title: Lévy bound for mapped random variables
statement: Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, let $(Omega,mu)$ and $(Xi,nu)$ be probability spaces, and let $U:Omegatobbr$ and $V:Xitobbr$ be measurable almost everywhere with respect to their respective measures. Suppose $Bge0$ and, for every $(m+1)$ times continuously differentiable function $phi:bbrtobbr$, every $Cge0$ bounding $|phi^{(m+1)}(t)|$ for all $t$, the absolute difference between the integrals of $phi(U)$ with respect to $mu$ and $phi(V)$ with respect to $nu$ is at most $CB$. Then the Lévy distance between the distributions of $U$ and $V$ is at most $((m+2)+2^m)B^{1/(m+2)}$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω and Ξ have measurable-space structures
μ on Ω and ν on Ξ are probability measures
U from Ω to ℝ is almost everywhere measurable with respect to μ
V from Ξ to ℝ is almost everywhere measurable with respect to ν
For every φ of class C^(m+1), every nonnegative C bounding its (m+1)st derivative everywhere, the absolute difference of the integrals of φ∘U and φ∘V is at most CB
